# Implement skill: run risk/effort evaluation rather than failing on the gate for plan_complete items missing risk/effort

Companion to ContextHub P4 (WL-0MTTSWCJR003OMN7, RCA WL-0MTTS9FY00055QJV) — related-to: WL-0MTTSWCJR003OMN7 (cross-repo companion, see ContextHub worklog). This is a SorraAgents-tracked work item (skill source lives in `skill/implement/` of this repo, symlinked to `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement`).

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher gates implement dispatch on `open/plan_complete` items having `risk ≤ Medium` and `effort ≤ Medium` (`classifyItemForDispatch` fails closed when risk/effort are absent). Items created without estimates are therefore **never implement-dispatchable** and no mechanism evaluates them (evidence: open_source_llm has 6 of 7 open plan_complete items with empty risk/effort — OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA et al.). The ContextHub dispatcher-side fix (P4) will either dispatch a risk/effort evaluation or adopt a default; either way the **implement skill** must behave correctly when invoked on (or alongside) an item whose estimates are missing — currently the effort/risk gate blocks the run instead of producing the missing data.

## Desired change

In the implement skill (`skill/implement/SKILL.md` and its scripts):
1. When starting implementation of a plan_complete item that lacks risk and/or effort, run the risk/effort evaluation (the effort-and-risk skill — `skill/effort-and-risk`/`effort_and_risk_skill`) **before/at gate time** and persist the estimates on the work item (wl update --risk/--effort), so the item is properly sized and the run proceeds — rather than failing on the gate.
2. Alternatively/additionally: when the dispatcher has already dispatched a standalone risk/effort evaluation for such an item, the implement skill accepts the item once estimates are present (no gate error).
3. Keep the gate for items WITH estimates (no behaviour change there); document the missing-estimate path in the SKILL.md and AGENTS guidance.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Invoking implement on a plan_complete item with empty risk/effort produces and persists risk/effort estimates and proceeds (or cleanly hands off to the evaluation), instead of refusing on the gate.
2. Estimates persist via `wl update` and the item becomes implement-dispatchable by the ContextHub dispatcher afterwards (cross-project fixture/step verified with OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA shape).
3. SKILL.md documents the missing-estimate flow; no regression for items with estimates.
4. Full project suite green (this repo).

## Key files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (+ `skill/implement/scripts/*`)
- `skill/effort-and-risk` (existing evaluation skill to reuse)

## Related

- ContextHub RCA WL-0MTTS9FY00055QJV and its P4 child (dispatcher-side); open_source_llm items OSL-0MSG7XUY0009OTVA, OSL-0MST3DPNF00812I3, OSL-0MSG7Y9TI000KDUO, OSL-0MSG7YB8U004C1RE, OSL-0MSG7YE3S0021DZT, OSL-0MSG7YFZG007IH3D (evidence)
data.title: Implement skill: run risk/effort evaluation rather than failing on the gate for plan_complete items missing risk/effort

## Context
The standup skill currently writes to stdout by default and only writes to a file when --output-path is supplied. The desired UX is to default to a dated file under ./standups/ so reports accumulate without manual path management.

## Goal
As an operator I want `python3 $(skill_path standup)/scripts/generate_standup.py` to write its report to `./standups/<year>_<month>_<day>.md` by default so that daily standup reports are persisted automatically.

## Work
- Change the default behaviour of `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` so that when `--output-path` is NOT provided it writes the rendered report to `./standups/<YYYY>_<MM>_<DD>.md` relative to the project root (the worklog's parent dir when --worklog-dir / WL_WORKLOG_DIR is set, otherwise cwd / cwd resolution).
- Ensure the target directory is created if it does not exist.
- Preserve explicit `--output-path <path>` override (when supplied, that path is used unchanged).
- Update `skill/standup/SKILL.md` Invocation docs to reflect the new default.
- Handle date as the report generation date (local datetime at generation time) formatted as zero-padded YYYY_MM_DD (e.g. 2026_09_10.md).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Running without --output-path writes a markdown report to ./standups/YYYY_MM_DD.md (e.g. ./standups/2026_09_10.md) using the current local date, creating ./standups/ if needed. (verified: manual smoke + test_default_path_writes_markdown_and_creates_dir)
- [x] Running with --output-path <path> still writes to that explicit path and does not also write to the default dated path. (verified: manual smoke + test_explicit_output_path_used_instead_of_default)
- [x] SKILL.md documents the new default ("./standups/YYYY_MM_DD.md" when --output-path omitted).
- [x] Existing flags (--json, --verbose, --worklog-dir, --count, --startTime, --duration) continue to work. (all 9 pre-existing standup tests pass unmodified; --json covered in new tests)
- [x] Tests cover both the default dated file path and the --output-path override. (8 new tests in test_generate_standup_default_output_path.py)

## Out of scope
- Changing the report contents/format beyond routing the output destination.
data.title: Standup writes to ./standups/YYYY_MM_DD.md by default

## Goal

Fix `_run_eslint_findings_check` and `_run_eslint_fix_mode` in `linter_runner.py` to filter file targets to JS/TS extensions before invoking eslint, preventing false parsing errors on `.py` and other non-JS/TS files.

## Root Cause

- `_run_eslint_findings_check` (line 351): `cmd = ["eslint", *[str(f) for f in files], "-f", "json", "--quiet"]` passes raw `files` with no extension filter.
- `_run_eslint_fix_mode` (lines 722, 727): same gap in both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd`.
- ESLint v6.4.0 tries to parse `.py` files as JavaScript and emits "Parsing error: Unterminated string constant".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Scoped eslint runs filter file targets to JS/TS extensions; a `.py`-only changed-file list produces zero eslint findings (eslint skipped or given no JS/TS targets).
- [ ] `_run_eslint_findings_check` filters `files` to JS/TS extensions (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`) before building the eslint command.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_findings_check` returns `[]` (skips eslint) when no JS/TS targets remain after filtering.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_fix_mode` filters both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd` to JS/TS extensions only.
- [ ] `_run_eslint_fix_mode` returns `(empty_findings, False)` when no JS/TS targets remain.
- [ ] Non-JS/TS files in the changed-file list are silently skipped (no false-positive findings).
- [ ] Whole-project mode (no explicit files list) is unaffected — it already defaults to JS extensions.

## Key Files

- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — functions to fix: `_run_eslint_findings_check`, `_run_eslint_fix_mode`
- `tests/test_linter_runner_eslint_filter.py` — unit tests (see SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ)

## Implementation Notes

- Add a constant `ESLINT_EXTENSIONS = (".js", ".jsx", ".mjs", ".cjs", ".ts", ".tsx")` near the top of the file (or inline in each function).
- In `_run_eslint_findings_check`, before building the command:

  ```python
  if files:
      js_files = [f for f in files if str(f).endswith(ESLINT_EXTENSIONS)]
      if not js_files:
          return []
      cmd = ["eslint", *[str(f) for f in js_files], "-f", "json", "--quiet"]
  else:
      cmd = ["eslint", str(root), "-f", "json", "--quiet"]
  ```

- In `_run_eslint_fix_mode`, apply the same filter in both `fix_cmd` and `rescan_cmd` closures.
- Follow the existing ruff guard pattern at line 392: `py_files = [f for f in files if str(f).endswith(("...",))]`

## Dependencies

- Depends on the unit tests SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ and the regression test SA-0MUDUW8CI008B73L (test-first ordering).
data.title: Fix: filter eslint to JS/TS extensions in scoped-lint path

## Goal

Add a regression/integration test proving that a scoped lint run whose changed-file scope contains only `.py` files completes without an eslint "Parsing error" blocking finding, exercising the real command-construction path (not mocked) with a stub runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An audit whose changed-file scope contains only `.py` files completes without an eslint "Parsing error" blocking finding (regression).
- [ ] The test invokes `run_eslint` (or the public linter entry point) with a `.py`-only `files` list and a stub `runner` that records the constructed command.
- [ ] Assertion: the recorded command contains no `.py` target (eslint is skipped entirely when no JS/TS files remain).
- [ ] No finding has `severity` of `"high"` or `"critical"` for the `.py`-only scope.
- [ ] Test lives in `tests/test_linter_runner_eslint_filter.py` (repository-standard code-quality test location, alongside `tests/test_code_quality_scoping.py`) and passes via the standard test runner.

## Key Files

- `skill/code_review/scripts/linter_runner.py` — public entry point(s) to exercise
- `tests/test_linter_runner_eslint_filter.py` — shared test module (`TestRunEslintScopedRegression`)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the unit tests SA-0MUDCVBXM009MFYJ (shared test module).
- This is a test-first item: authored before implementation; it fails until SA-0MUDD7BHE006V3RI lands, which depends on this item.

## Implementation Notes

- Use a stub `runner` callable that returns a controlled result and records the command list, so the test asserts real filtering behaviour without requiring eslint on PATH.
- Assert the `.py` path never appears in any eslint invocation command.
